issues.legal_issue: Trees attached to land are not crops or other products raised on the land requiring notice of forfeiture before forfeiture under the land-conservancy provision.
material_facts: The claimant planted trees on land treated as government land and was later evicted from it.
No notice of forfeiture was given to the claimant.
The provision refers to a crop or other product raised on the land, and the court read “other product” in the context of “crop.”
issues.conclusion: Trees are not “other products raised on the land” within the provision, so the government was not required to give notice of forfeiture of the trees under that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 9 of the Travancore Land Conservancy Act, 1916, “other product” is read in the context of “crop”; the words “raised on the land” qualify both expressions. The provision concerns products of a nature similar to crops, grown and gathered in a season, rather than trees attached to the land. The court applied Clark and Another v. Gaskarth, 8 Taunt 431.

predicates.appeal_from_improvements_compensation_cl: A person appeals a decision on a claim for compensation for improvements made to land.
predicates.trees_attached_to_land: The disputed improvements include trees planted on the land that remain attached to it.
predicates.forfeiture_notice_absent: The authority did not give the occupier a notice forfeiting the disputed property.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns compensation for improvements and the disputed property consists of trees attached to land, the absence of a forfeiture notice does not make such notice necessary for those trees.

issues.legal_issue: A deliberate trespasser who improves land while knowing that they have no right to occupy it is not entitled to compensation for trees planted on the land merely because they intended to improve it.
material_facts: The claimant’s possession began after an application to register the land had been rejected.
The claimant made the improvements after that rejection, knowing that ownership of the land was disputed and that the government claimed it.
The claimant had no bona fide claim of title and entered or remained on the land without permission.
The claimant argued that a bona fide intention to improve the land entitled a trespasser to compensation.
The claim concerned the value of trees planted on the land after the claimant was evicted.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled under general law to compensation for the trees; an intention to improve the land does not turn a deliberate, wrongful trespass into a compensable one.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5 of the Travancore Land Conservancy Act, 1916 prohibited occupation of government land without permission, and section 6 made contravention punishable. The maxim quicquid plantatur solo, solo cedit does not apply in India, but that does not give a wrongful trespasser a right to trees planted on another’s land. The court applied Vallabdas Narainji v. Development Officer, Bandra, A.I.R. 1929 P.C. 163, which did not establish that a mere deliberate trespasser is entitled to compensation. The court also reasoned that a trespasser’s position cannot be better than that of a lawful tenant who has lost possession and cannot claim compensation for improvements.

rule.if: appeal_from_improvements_compensation_claim and deliberate_unauthorised_occupation and knowledge_of_lack_of_right and trees_planted_by_occupier

predicates.appeal_from_improvements_compensation_cl: A person appeals a decision on a claim for compensation for improvements made to land.
predicates.deliberate_unauthorised_occupation: The claimant deliberately occupied land without permission.
predicates.knowledge_of_lack_of_right: When occupying or improving the land, the claimant knew they had no right or title to do so.
predicates.trees_planted_by_occupier: The claimant planted the trees for which compensation is sought.

issues.definition: If a claimant appeals a compensation decision after deliberately occupying land without permission, knowing they lacked a right to it, and planting the trees claimed for, the output is that compensation for those trees is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A contention that an occupier was evicted without notice cannot be raised for the first time on appeal when it was not clearly pleaded or made an issue in the courts below.
material_facts: The claimant argued before the Supreme Court that no notice to quit had been given and that this prevented removal of the trees.
The plaint did not clearly allege eviction without notice, and its allegations about lacking an opportunity to remove improvements referred to other items.
No issue about lack of eviction notice was framed at trial, and no application to frame such an issue was made in the trial court, the High Court, or the Supreme Court.
The courts found that the claimant had deliberately occupied the land knowing that they had no right to enter it and had been rightly evicted.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not permitted to raise the contention about lack of eviction notice for the first time before the Supreme Court.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to entertain a new appellate contention that was not clearly pleaded and was not made an issue in the courts below. The claimant’s testimony about not receiving notice did not overcome the failure to plead or seek an issue on that point, particularly in light of the findings that the occupation was deliberate and the eviction was rightful.

rule.if: appeal_to_supreme_court and eviction_without_notice_contention_new_on_appeal and contention_not_clearly_pleaded and no_lower_court_issue_framed and deliberate_unauthorised_occupation

predicates.appeal_to_supreme_court: A party appeals to the Supreme Court from a decision concerning eviction and a claim for improvements.
predicates.eviction_without_notice_contention_new_o: The appellant first argues in the Supreme Court that eviction occurred without notice.
predicates.contention_not_clearly_pleaded: The pleadings do not clearly allege that the appellant was evicted without notice.
predicates.no_lower_court_issue_framed: No issue about lack of eviction notice was framed in the lower courts, and no application to frame one was made there.
predicates.deliberate_unauthorised_occupation: The courts found that the appellant deliberately occupied land knowing they had no right to do so.

issues.definition: When an appellant first raises lack of eviction notice in the Supreme Court, did not clearly plead it or obtain a lower-court issue on it, and deliberately occupied the land without a right, the contention is not entertained.
